arXiv:math/0609442v1 [math.PR] 15 Sep 2006

Convexity of the median in the gamma distribution

Christian Berg    Henrik L. Pedersen Note: Research supported by the Carlsberg Foundation
August 24, 2026
Abstract

We show that the median m⁡(x)m(x) in the gamma distribution with parameter xx is a strictly convex function on the positive half-line.

2000 Mathematics Subject Classification:
primary 60E05; secondary 41A60, 33B15.

Keywords: median, gamma function, gamma distribution.

1 Introduction

The median of the gamma distribution with (positive) parameter xx is defined implicitly by the formula

∫0m⁡(x)e−t​tx−1​𝑑t=12​∫0∞e−t​tx−1​𝑑t.\int_{0}^{m(x)}e^{-t}t^{x-1}\,dt=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t}t^{x-1}\,dt. (1)

In a recent paper (see [5]) we showed the 0<m′​(x)<10<m^{\prime}(x)<1 for all x>0x>0. Consequently, m⁡(x)−xm(x)-x is a decreasing function, which for x=1,2,…x=1,2,\ldots yields a positive answer to the Chen-Rubin conjecture. Other authors have solved this conjecture in its discrete setting (see [2], [1], [3]).

In [4] convexity of the sequence m⁡(n+1)m(n+1) has been established, and the natural question arises if m⁡(x)m(x) is a convex function. The main result of this paper is the following.

Theorem 1.1

The median m⁡(x)m(x) defined in (1) satisfies m′′​(x)>0m^{\prime\prime}(x)>0. In particular it is a strictly convex function for x>0x>0.
